markdown_report:
At 10% progress, prioritize a small, falsifiable GRU4Rec intervention: an item-conditioned gate on the existing recurrent carry term.

The starting evidence yields three insights. Older isolated interests and insufficient priority for recent repeated behavior motivate selective forgetting, but do not prove excessive retention. All four categories fail final-feature consistency despite zero reported aligned-feature and candidate-score discrepancies; diagnose this independently before interpreting temporal effects. Movies’ sampled negative-beats-positive rate is 7.01% for frequency 1–4 versus 1.51% for 20+, identifying a descriptive sparse-item weakness, not its cause.

Related work suggests three directions. GRU4Rec’s BPR-max emphasizes competitive negatives without guaranteeing generalization [1]. TSSR motivates content–interaction alignment, although scratch-trained text effectiveness remains unestablished [2]. Hierarchical Multiscale RNNs and LSTM forget gates establish adaptive memory management; selective forgetting is therefore established prior work [3,5].

| Direction | Mechanism | Unresolved gap |
|---|---|---|
| Memory | Item-conditioned carry attenuation | Forgetting useful persistent preferences |
| Representation | Jointly trained title pooling | Sparse supervision and textual shortcuts |
| Objective | Matched-pool BPR-max | Hard negatives and false negatives |

Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Ratings reflect hypotheses rather than measured gains.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Item-only carry gate** | **2/5/7/5/5** | Compact conditional forgetting targets stale-interest revival and recent-pattern underweighting; sampled errors are measurable. | Established gating, possible gradient attenuation, custom recurrence and export work. |
| Scratch-trained title pooling | 4/6/6/6/5 | Shared words may improve specificity and sparse-item separation. | Titles cannot establish current intent; textual shortcuts and integration add risk. |
| Matched-pool BPR-max | 2/7/4/7/3 | Established objective targets competitive ranking errors. | No direct mechanism for both required user failures; sampling confounds attribution. |

Select the carry gate for feasibility and explicit coverage of both user failures. Compute ordinary GRU update z and candidate n, then h=z·r(x)·h_previous+(1−z)·n, with r(x)=sigmoid(Wx+b), W=0 and b=log(99). Unlike whole-state pre-gating, this preserves ordinary reset/candidate calculations [4]. Coefficients sum to at most one: the added mechanism permits forgetting toward zero without increasing candidate weight. It neither guarantees reduced state norm nor improved intent matching. Long retention requires both gates near one; additional direct-path gradient attenuation may harm persistent preferences.

Target residual sampled ranking errors, especially Movies’ 4.29% overall error. Execution repair is a separate prerequisite, never an architectural gain. Verify fixed-r=1 forward/gradient equivalence before training. Where budget permits, compare constant attenuation, learned constant-vector retention and item-conditioned retention under matched settings; otherwise limit attribution. Inspect frequency/history-length slices and gate shortcuts without replacing official macro validation HR@10 selection. Preserve one checkpoint per category, fixed seeds, splits and evaluator. No improvement is claimed; sampled ranking gains need not transfer to full-catalog rankings [6].

References: [1] [GRU4Rec](https://github.com/hidasib/GRU4Rec); [2] [TSSR](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.07623); [3] [HM-RNN](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.01704); [4] [PyTorch GRU](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.GRU.html); [5] [LSTM forgetting](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11032042/); [6] [Sampled metrics](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/).

idea.description: Replace the starting whole-state retention gate with an item-only gate on the existing GRU carry term in the first recurrent layer. The ordinary GRU reset gate, update gate and candidate retain their supplied definitions. All parameters train jointly within exactly one network per category; inference loads one checkpoint per category. This is an incremental selective-forgetting hypothesis, not a claim of a novel forgetting principle.
idea.motivation: Selective carry attenuation explicitly targets older isolated interests persisting and recent repeated behavior receiving insufficient priority. Item-conditioned attenuation can learn different persistence for observed items without claiming access to intent, ownership, compatibility or mood. Residual sampled ranking errors provide the model-facing target, particularly Movies' 4.29% overall negative-beats-positive rate and its 7.01% rate for training-frequency 1–4 versus 1.51% for 20+. Unresolved final-feature discrepancies require an independent execution investigation; the added gate is not their proposed repair. These mechanisms and benefits remain hypotheses. Title pooling remains a plausible later direction for specificity and sparse items; BPR-max remains a plausible separate objective experiment, but neither should be combined with the initial gate intervention.
idea.implementation_notes:
Integrate into the supplied corrected baseline; its source and numeric hyperparameters are absent here, so the code below specifies the recurrence intervention rather than inventing a replacement training pipeline. Preserve existing dimensions, layers, input/output transformations, dropout, sampler, objective, optimizer and checkpoint schedule. Record their resolved values, actual training precision and runtime settings in the trial configuration. Do not combine this intervention with text features or a new loss in the initial experiment. The supplied earlier combined scores are contextual evidence, not a fresh paired comparison under this proposal.

Add exactly one H-by-input_dimension projection with bias to the first recurrent layer. Its input is that layer's existing current item-ID input representation, including the baseline's existing transformations. Initialize weights to zero and bias to log(99), giving initial retention 0.99 in exact arithmetic. Leave all higher layers unchanged. The earlier suggestion of adding a gate to every layer is superseded by this first-layer-only specification. Record layer index zero and the baseline's recurrent convention. Shared baseline parameter tensors must begin identically; adding a module must not shift initialization draws or subsequent sampling/dropout randomness. Construct the extra module inside torch.random.fork_rng, restoring CPU and any involved CUDA RNG states. A newly constructed nn.Linear consumes random draws even when immediately overwritten. Preserve baseline construction order; do not reseed the entire pipeline after adding the gate.

For PyTorch's reset-after-linear convention and gate order (r,z,n), compute reset=sigmoid(i_r+h_r), update=sigmoid(i_z+h_z), candidate=tanh(i_n+reset*h_n), and proposed=update*retention*previous+(1-update)*candidate. The reset multiplies the recurrent candidate bias as well as its matrix contribution. Do not move reset before the recurrent matrix. If the supplied baseline uses another documented convention, retain that convention and modify only its direct carry term. Preserve baseline input, output and between-layer dropout placement. Built-in GRU dropout acts between stacked recurrent layers and excludes the last layer; it does not provide internal dropout for a single-layer GRU. A custom implementation must reproduce the baseline's effective dropout behavior rather than silently adding, dropping or relocating it.

Algebraically the intervention subtracts update*(1-retention)*previous from the ordinary GRU update. Effective carry and write coefficients are f=update*retention and i=1-update, satisfying f+i<=1. The missing mass is interpretable as interpolation toward zero, but cancellation or reinforcement with the candidate means total hidden-state norm need not decrease. Holding gate and candidate dependencies fixed, the direct carry-path Jacobian changes from diag(update) to diag(update*retention). This is not the full temporal Jacobian, which also contains derivatives of gates and candidates. Long retention requires both gates near one; useful long-term preferences and gradients may be lost. Initial retention 0.99 is not identity initialization, and its isolated extra carry factor is 0.99^k across k valid steps, without implying that full states decay at this rate. Monitor near-one saturation and weak conditioning gradients.

Padding must leave recurrent state unchanged and produce zero padded diagnostic features. Extract the greatest nonzero position from the original left-padded sequence, never count-1. Preserve the host empty-history fallback, including learned score biases. Investigate existing final-feature discrepancies using a single captured feature tensor, an independent maximum-position gather, raw hidden state versus transformed recommendation features, and repeated identical execution before batched-versus-singleton checks. The reported maximum errors range from 0.0001633 to 0.0006332 and do not prove an indexing bug. Keep atol=1e-5 and rtol=1e-4; unresolved execution failures leave temporal metrics null. Report absolute/relative errors and any score/rank effects rather than silently relaxing thresholds. Any necessary correction must be explicit and common to compared configurations, with retraining if semantics change.

Before a training run, verify custom ordinary recurrence with retention fixed to one against the supplied GRU using copied parameters, disabled dropout, identical valid chronological inputs and identical upstream gradients. Compare sequence outputs, final states, input gradients, initial-state gradients and recurrent parameter gradients. Check both this mathematical implementation equivalence and the separate padding/production-readout contract. Different kernels need not be bitwise identical, but unexplained failures at the declared tolerances remain failures. Check empty, singleton, mixed-length, maximum-length and standalone all-padding cases, batch permutation and added leading padding. If packing is used, compact real items into contiguous chronological prefixes, pack only nonempty rows, then scatter outputs back; never pack original left-padded rows with their valid counts or invent a recurrent step for empties.

Keep log2feats(sequence), item_emb, predict_score(features, items), score_candidates and ModelView compatible, including B x L x K candidate scoring. view.model remains the actual trained nn.Module. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader) returning metrics and metric_definitions, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). The interpreter must use measured metrics and definitions without inventing unavailable fields. The loader continues yielding (None, sequence, positive, negative), each B x L. Preserve user_train, meta_data and review_data interfaces even when fields are unavailable. Preserve existing measured margins, frequency slices and execution definitions. Collect added-gate quantiles and saturation fractions on valid positions through an optional temporary hook, reporting counts, thresholds and the checkpoint used. Use a fixed diagnostic batch set where supported; do not consume the training sampler's RNG stream or change training order while collecting probes. Gate values do not establish useful forgetting.

Rerun the existing temporal probe only after execution passes; do not change its populations, candidates, interventions or definitions to obtain favorable results. Keep temporal results null on unresolved execution failure. Near-midpoint mapped embedding cosine does not demonstrate recommendation diversity or rule out every form of representation collapse. Training-margin and temporal probes use training histories and do not establish validation generalization.

The mandatory experiment trains exactly one independent challenger model per category. Keep the ordinary corrected baseline as a reference only where an authorized measured reference exists; do not read other trials or reuse their checkpoints. Fixed-retention-one is a pretraining implementation check, not a required additional fit. If the experiment controller permits additional trials and sufficient shared budget remains, prioritize separately retrained fixed-r=0.99 and learned constant-vector retention controls before further architecture changes. Initialize the learned constant vector at log(99), matching the challenger's starting retention. These controls distinguish fixed attenuation, trainable item-independent attenuation and input conditioning, but do not isolate every capacity or optimization difference. A learned scalar is a lower-capacity alternative, not an additional mandatory sweep. Each control remains one jointly trained model per category and is never combined with another predictor. If controls are unrun, do not attribute any improvement specifically to item conditioning or superiority over a tuned constant.

Charge every authorized fit, diagnosis, debugging attempt and failure to the remaining shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Never assume the entire budget remains available. Before any optional trial, record configuration order, remaining allocation, intended completed-update budget and checkpoint opportunities. Do not launch additional configurations without sufficient allocation for a meaningful four-category comparison. Retain the host checkpoint schedule; compare matched completed training/evaluation opportunities when making controlled claims, and report truncation or unequal opportunities explicitly. Architecture-equivalence checks and execution diagnosis also consume the shared budget. Custom recurrence can lose fused-GRU throughput; measure synchronized step time and memory rather than assuming the parameter count predicts runtime.

Check for shortcut learning by summarizing retention and ranking errors against training-only item frequency, retained-history length and valid chronological position. Where enough observations exist, cross-stratify frequency and history length; report subgroup counts and sparse cells. These correlations are descriptive and cannot establish causal intent recovery. Item-conditioned gates may encode popular-item shortcuts or excessive recency, and repeated preferences may require retention rather than attenuation. If the unchanged host evaluator already exposes target IDs, histories and per-user validation hits, report supplementary validation HR@10 and paired hit differences by training-only target-frequency bands 1–4, 5–19 and 20+, and prespecified history-length bins 1–5, 6–10, 11–20 and >20. Mark zero-training-frequency targets separately if present. Do not modify the evaluator or infer unavailable paired outcomes to produce these slices. They are diagnostic summaries, never replacement selection metrics or guarantees of full-catalog quality.

Retain Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl routing; DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; preprocessing seed 0; training seed 42; at most 200 epochs; exactly 200 batches per completed epoch; single-GPU execution; and artifacts beneath the trial directory. Preserve supplied splits, evaluator, checkpoint schedule and official macro validation HR@10 selection with 200 users per category, 99 unique negatives and evaluation seed 42. Do not manufacture paired outcomes or uncertainty from aggregate scores. Keep the separate native full-catalog recommendations for five real training users per category, and use only supplied simulator judgments when discussing the two user-facing failures. Track unjudgeable item content separately from explicit preference mismatch. This ID-only gate cannot resolve absent compatibility specifications, ownership needs or desired mood.

Save architecture version, gate location, dimensions, baseline transformations, dropout/scoring configuration and state_dict in each category checkpoint. A learned gate's final retention is determined by its saved parameters; its initialization bias alone is not a runtime substitute. Update the predictor writer with the identical recurrence and final-feature extraction. Verify selected in-memory, reloaded and embedded-predictor scores agree on identical histories and candidates, including empty histories and supported candidate shapes. Each route loads exactly one model/checkpoint; no score fusion, independently fitted components or averaging. Use no hidden tests, extra datasets, pretrained weights, other-trial checkpoints, unavailable ratings/reviews/categories/prices/stores or inferred simulator traits.

Originality is revised to 2/10 because independent forgetting is established and carry-only gating already appears in the supplied inspirations; novelty of this exact parameterization is unverified. Future potential is 5/10 because the experiment can clarify a constrained retention tradeoff, while existing GRU gates may already suffice. Code difficulty is 5/10: the added projection is small, but faithful custom recurrence, gradients, dropout, runtime, diagnostics and embedded export make the full intervention moderately demanding.
idea.pseudocode:
import math
import torch
from torch import nn
from torch.nn import functional as F


class ItemCarryGate(nn.Module):
    """Added gate for layer zero; construct with RNG preservation below."""
    def __init__(self, input_size, hidden_size):
        super().__init__()
        self.proj = nn.Linear(input_size, hidden_size)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.proj.weight)
        nn.init.constant_(self.proj.bias, math.log(99.0))

    def forward(self, x):
        return torch.sigmoid(self.proj(x))


def make_gate_without_advancing_rng(input_size, hidden_size, reference):
    # Construct on CPU within a saved CPU RNG context. Moving an already
    # initialized module to the reference device does not initialize it again.
    # For direct CUDA construction, fork the relevant CUDA device RNG too.
    with torch.random.fork_rng(devices=[]):
        gate = ItemCarryGate(input_size, hidden_size)
    return gate.to(device=reference.device, dtype=reference.dtype)


def carry_gated_step(x, h, weight_ih, weight_hh,
                     bias_ih, bias_hh, retention):
    """PyTorch reset-after-linear convention, gate order (r, z, n).

    Reuse baseline parameters; do not reinitialize them. Preserve existing
    dropout and transforms at their original sites outside this step.
    For a different supplied convention, preserve that convention instead.
    """
    i_r, i_z, i_n = F.linear(x, weight_ih, bias_ih).chunk(3, dim=-1)
    h_r, h_z, h_n = F.linear(h, weight_hh, bias_hh).chunk(3, dim=-1)
    reset = torch.sigmoid(i_r + h_r)
    update = torch.sigmoid(i_z + h_z)
    candidate = torch.tanh(i_n + reset * h_n)
    return update * retention * h + (1.0 - update) * candidate


def masked_step(x, previous, valid, gru_parameters, gate):
    proposed = carry_gated_step(
        x, previous, *gru_parameters, retention=gate(x))
    state = torch.where(valid[:, None], proposed, previous)
    features = torch.where(valid[:, None], state, torch.zeros_like(state))
    return state, features


def final_nonpadding_features(sequence, features):
    batch, width = sequence.shape
    if width == 0:
        return features.new_zeros((batch, features.shape[-1]))
    positions = torch.arange(width, device=sequence.device)[None, :]
    last = torch.where(sequence.ne(0), positions, -1).amax(dim=1)
    result = features.gather(
        1, last.clamp_min(0)[:, None, None].expand(
            -1, 1, features.shape[-1])).squeeze(1)
    return torch.where(last[:, None].ge(0), result, torch.zeros_like(result))


# Host integration: reuse the corrected training pipeline, not a new pipeline.
# DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']
# Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42 and all four category routes.
# Record inherited configuration, remaining shared budget and checkpoint schedule.
#
# Before training:
#   Diagnose final-feature execution independently of the intervention.
#   Copy baseline GRU parameters into the custom ordinary recurrence.
#   With dropout disabled and retention=ones_like(previous), compare outputs,
#   final states and input/initial-state/parameter gradients against the baseline.
#   Use identical upstream gradients; atol=1e-5, rtol=1e-4.
#   Verify padding, empty-row policy and original-coordinate final readout.
#   Do not reinterpret prior checkpoints under changed recurrence semantics.
#
# For each category:
#   Reset the host category training RNGs exactly as the baseline does (seed 42).
#   Construct the corrected baseline with unchanged initialization order.
#   Attach make_gate_without_advancing_rng(...) AFTER baseline initialization.
#   Add gate parameters to the baseline optimizer with its existing settings.
#   Preserve the baseline's parameter treatment and document any grouping.
#   Run chronological masked recurrence with this gate only on layer zero.
#   Higher layers and recommendation transformations remain unchanged.
#   log2feats returns actual recommendation features at original positions.
#   Train unchanged loss/sampler for <=200 completed epochs,
#   exactly 200 batches per completed epoch, within the remaining shared budget.
#   Apply the existing checkpoint-selection schedule and pinned evaluator.
#   Serialize one selected checkpoint with complete architecture configuration.
#
# Update the embedded predictor WRITER with the same recurrence and readout;
# preserve all four routes and baseline scoring biases/activations.
# Verify actual model / ModelView / reloaded / embedded-predictor score agreement.
#
# Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and
# diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Return measured metrics and
# metric_definitions; keep loader tuples (None, sequence, positive, negative).
# Collect valid-position gate statistics on fixed diagnostic batches without
# advancing training RNGs; report counts, saturation thresholds and frequency /
# history-length / chronological-position slices where supported.
# Leave temporal metrics null unless all execution checks pass.
#
# Optional separately authorized controls, only within remaining shared budget:
#   fixed retention 0.99; learned constant-vector retention initialized to 0.99.
# Retrain matched controls separately; never combine their scores/checkpoints.
# Without controls, do not claim conditioning caused an observed improvement.
# Select only by unchanged official four-category macro validation HR@10.
# Report optional validation slices only from host-exposed data; invent nothing.
# Keep the separate native twenty-user full-catalog recommendation procedure.
#
# This is an integration module, not a standalone replacement train.py.

originality.positive: The first-layer, item-only carry intervention defines a precise and testable adaptation with explicit constant-retention controls.
originality.negative: Independent forgetting predates this proposal, and carry-only gating already appears in the supplied inspirations; novelty of the exact parameterization is unverified.

future_potential.positive: A controlled experiment could clarify whether conditional carry attenuation improves the retention tradeoff beyond ordinary GRU gates and item-independent decay.
future_potential.negative: The gate may duplicate existing behavior, encode popularity shortcuts or attenuate useful long-term gradients; no validation benefit or recovery of latent intent is established.

code_difficulty.positive: The trainable addition is one small projection, uses existing item inputs and requires no new datasets, external weights or independently fitted scorer.
code_difficulty.negative: Faithful recurrence and gradient equivalence, dropout semantics, RNG preservation, execution diagnosis, runtime control and embedded-predictor consistency require moderate integration work.

related_work.title: Official GRU4Rec implementation
contributions: Provides recurrent recommendation objectives including BPR-max and cross-entropy.
Motivates a separate matched-negative-pool objective comparison.
limitations: Does not establish that an added carry gate improves this benchmark.
Objective comparisons require matched sampling and compute to isolate their effects.

related_work.title: TSSR — supplied text and collaborative alignment reference
contributions: The supplied search summary motivates aligning item content with interaction representations rather than relying on textual similarity alone.
limitations: The supplied summary does not establish effectiveness for a small text encoder trained from scratch under this task's constraints.
This is a deferred representation direction, not evidence for the selected carry gate.

related_work.title: Hierarchical Multiscale Recurrent Neural Networks
contributions: Introduces learned boundaries controlling recurrent update, copy and flush operations.
Provides precedent for learning memory-management decisions without boundary labels.
limitations: Its language and handwriting experiments do not establish recommendation gains.
The proposed continuous item-only carry gate is an adaptation, not a reproduction of its architecture.

related_work.title: Learning Phrase Representations using RNN Encoder–Decoder for Statistical Machine Translation
contributions: Provides foundational gated recurrent equations and the distinction between update and reset mechanisms.
limitations: Does not evaluate this additional carry attenuation or the RecHarness task.
Implementation conventions must be checked against the supplied backbone rather than inferred from a general GRU equation.

related_work.title: Learning to Forget: Continual Prediction with LSTM
contributions: Establishes learned forgetting of recurrent stored state independently of writing.
Limits novelty claims for the proposed selective-forgetting mechanism.
limitations: LSTM cell-state dynamics differ from the proposed GRU hidden-state intervention.
Does not establish recommendation benefits or novelty of this exact parameterization.

related_work.title: PyTorch GRU documentation
contributions: Specifies reset-after-linear candidate computation, gate ordering and stacked-layer dropout behavior.
Provides the implementation reference for ordinary-recurrence equivalence checks.
limitations: Different execution kernels can produce floating-point differences.
Documentation alone does not verify the host model's transformations, padding behavior or predictor implementation.

related_work.title: PyTorch random-number generation documentation
contributions: Documents fork_rng for preserving CPU and selected device RNG states around extra module construction.
limitations: Does not preserve Python or NumPy RNG state.
Does not cancel randomness used later by a changed forward path or altered training schedule.

related_work.title: PyTorch Linear implementation
contributions: Shows that Linear construction invokes parameter initialization and therefore consumes RNG before explicit zeroing.
limitations: Implementation details should be matched to the installed PyTorch version.
Preserving construction RNG alone does not guarantee matched training trajectories.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking metrics can disagree with full-catalog comparisons.
Supports limiting claims to the pinned sampled-candidate benchmark.
limitations: Does not justify changing the required evaluator or selection metric.
Does not determine whether this particular carry-gate comparison will reverse under full-catalog evaluation.

related_work.title: Sequential-recommendation sampling study — supplied Prakash et al. reference
contributions: The supplied search summary reports dataset-dependent accuracy and popularity tradeoffs across negative-sampling methods.
Motivates descriptive training-frequency strata alongside aggregate validation results.
limitations: Does not establish that retention gates improve tail-item ranking.
Subgroup analysis requires host-exposed outcomes and adequate counts; it cannot replace official macro validation selection.
